conviction_note: Peer read-through (HAL's Q3 Middle East/Asia +8% q/q on Saudi and Kuwait, Mexico up) and a bar lowered by a 21% drawdown since 31 Aug plus four October target cuts point mildly up. Against that sits the arithmetic of the FY26 EBITDA guide, which needs a ~17% q/q Q4 ramp that management already said was shrinking. So p_up is 54, abs_move 6.5 (between the 4.15 median reaction and the 8.23 implied move from a thin chain, raised because a FY guide revision is likely), and the scaled number is +0.52 against an impact_sum of +0.20. They are close because the guidance negative and the read-through positives roughly offset.
bar: Revenue $1.13B: Q3 guide $1.105-1.155B (midpoint $1.13B, call transcript https://www.webull.com/news/15271277430924288), matched by MarketBeat ($1.13B, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-weatherford-international-wfrd-expected-to-release-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-10-13/) and Benzinga ($1.13-1.14B). Adjusted EBITDA guide $235-265M with margins up at least 100bp q/q; adjusted FCF guide >$100M; FY26 EBITDA guide $951M-$1,046M. The GAAP EPS bar is disputed: $1.30 MarketBeat, $1.26 Benzinga, $1.20 Earnings Whispers. EPS-dependent findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 4.17M shares, 5.95% of float, 4.0 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 record date (FINRA, published 2026-10-09). Prior period 2026-09-15: 4.13M, 4.31 days. Source: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/WFRD/short-interest/. Not a crowded short. Baseline 25d skew +1.84 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.85, total front-expiry OI only 493 with the ATM spread at 18% of mid, so the 8.23% implied move rests on a thin chain. Tape: spot 78.6, about 21% below the $97.77 close of 2026-08-31 used in the NCS merger (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001692427/000119312526377638/d534761d8k.htm), -6.4% over 20 days, -29% from the 52-week high. October target cuts: Goldman 106->94 (10-14), Piper 118->110, Citi 115->112 (10-19), UBS 120->116 (09-23). Insiders sold about $2.24M in the quarter (two directors).

findings.finding: Halliburton's Q3 2026 release (Oct 20, before the open) shows Middle East/Asia revenue of $1.4B, up 8% sequentially on higher activity across multiple product lines in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, with Q4 Middle East guided up both q/q and y/y. WFRD's MENA/Asia segment, 40% of its revenue ($446M in Q2, -6% q/q on the Iran conflict), is the line its Q2 miss came from, and management last spoke on Jul 21, when it said a recent flare-up had added uncertainty. Net of the rest of the company: HAL's North America fell 5% q/q, and WFRD has its own Saudi drag from the end of an LSTK contract, which is already in its guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (Middle East-driven EPS miss, $0.55 vs ~$0.90; revenue beat $1.10B vs $1.07B): stock +4.55%. Q2 2025: +4.76%. 6 of 7 recent prints closed up.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer print came out this morning and WFRD is +2% today (78.6 vs 77.09), so part of it is already in the price. If all of it were priced, WFRD would have retraced a meaningful part of its 21% drawdown instead of a 2% day, and the four October target cuts (the latest on 10-19) would not have been written into the print. Consensus revenue is still sitting exactly at the guide midpoint, set before HAL spoke.
findings.independence: Same Halliburton release and call as the Mexico finding below (a different number in the same document). HAL's call (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-what-halliburton-hal-said-on-its-q3-earnings-call-2026-10-20/) and TT News (https://www.ttnews.com/articles/halliburton-earnings-q3-2026) add a multi-year rebuild narrative and a 2027 framework with the Middle East in line with 2H26. Counter: WFRD's own Jul 21 call flagged Saudi LSTK roll-off and Indonesia declines (https://www.webull.com/news/15271277430924288).

findings.finding: Halliburton's Q3 Latin America revenue was flat at $1.1B, with weaker Argentina stimulation offset by 'increased activity across multiple product service lines in Mexico'. WFRD's Q2 Latin America revenue fell 12% q/q to $197M, mainly from lower Mexico drilling and ISP activity and deferred wells, and management expected Pemex's calendar to normalise in the second half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mexico and Pemex have been the swing line for WFRD's collections and LatAm revenue. Q3 2025, when no Pemex payments arrived: +0.64%. The stock has not shown an isolated reaction to Mexico revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a sub-line in a peer release from the same morning. If it were priced, WFRD's LatAm segment (~18% of revenue) would already be modelled as recovering, which does not fit a revenue consensus sitting at the guide midpoint. Net of the rest: LatAm is under a fifth of revenue, so even a 10% q/q rebound adds only ~$20M.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the finding above. WFRD's own Jul 21 call said Pemex activity should normalise in H2 and grow mid-to-high single digits in 2027 (https://www.webull.com/news/15271277430924288). Pemex supplier complaints of Sep 23, 2026 (https://www.poresto.com/campeche/2026/9/28/pemex-y-ciudad-del-carmen-que-paso-con-los-adeudos-a-empresas-y-trabajadores.html) concern old arrears, not activity.

findings.finding: The FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide of $951M-$1,046M, set on Jul 21, implies a steep Q4. H1 was about $456M (Q1 $233M + Q2 $223M), so H2 must be $495M-$590M. Against the Q3 guide of $235M-$265M, that leaves Q4 at $230M-$325M (midpoint ~$293M, +17% over the Q3 midpoint). Management had already cut the year by about 1% in July, said the H2 margin step-up would be smaller than planned in April, and said the Middle East impact would grow over the year. A FY cut toward or below the low end on this print is the main downside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 21, 2026: FY trimmed ~1% at the midpoint, FCF conversion raised: +4.55%. Apr 22, 2025, when the tariff/macro guide reset hit: -7.18%, the only large down reaction in the 7-print history.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is down 21% since Aug 31 and four brokers cut targets in the last month, which is what a market braced for a guide cut looks like. Not fully priced because the formal FY range still stands, and a cut to the low end implies a Q4 EBITDA of ~$250M, flat with Q3. HAL's Q4 Middle East guide (up q/q) cuts against the size of a cut.
findings.independence: Q1 EBITDA of $233M comes from the Q1 2026 coverage (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/weatherford-wfrd-q1-2026-earnings-152938139.html). Q2 figures come from the 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001603923/000160392326000082/a2026-q2ex991earningsrelea.htm). The October target cuts (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-weatherford-international-nasdaq-wfrd-stock-price-target-lowered-at-citigroup-2026-10-19/) point the same way. HAL's Q4 Middle East outlook points the other way.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP EPS faces one-off charges that the disputed $1.20-1.30 consensus may not carry. NCS Multistage closed on Sep 1, 2026, and its credit facility was paid off at close. In Q2, WFRD booked $25M of 'other charges', mainly redomestication and M&A costs, plus $9M of restructuring. The Delaware redomestication was approved on Sep 3 and still awaits the Irish High Court. A rough GAAP walk at $250M EBITDA with $15-25M of charges lands near $1.10-1.20.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GAAP EPS of $0.55 missed ~$0.90 by $0.35, driven by $34M of charges and a $33M tax swing, and the stock rose 4.55%. This name has not paid for GAAP EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS bar is not settled (three sources, $1.20-$1.30). But the market demonstrably looks through charges on this name, so the finding is small on purpose. The charge size is my inference, not a disclosed number.
findings.independence: Q2 charges and the redomestication status are in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001603923/000160392326000082/a2026-q2ex991earningsrelea.htm) and the Sep 3 vote result (https://finviz.com/news/388930/weatherford-shareholders-approve-redomestication-to-delaware).

findings.finding: Chief Accounting Officer Desmond Mills gave notice on Sep 2 and resigned effective Oct 16, 2026, four days before the Q3 print, 'to pursue another opportunity'. He was replaced by the Treasurer, Maximiliano Kricorian, a 13-year Weatherford veteran and CPA. The Q3 close is therefore signed under a new CAO.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CAO change found in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: It was a quiet Item 5.02 8-K with no wire coverage found. It is an inference, not evidence of an accounting problem: an internal successor and a stated reason argue for an ordinary departure, so it is sized near zero.

findings.finding: NCS Multistage closed on Sep 1, 2026, so Q3 carries about one month of NCS. NCS's Q2 revenue was $38.4M at a ~5% adjusted EBITDA margin, so roughly $12-14M of revenue and ~$0.5M of EBITDA land in Q3. The revenue guide was given Jul 21, while the deal was still pending. The effect is a slight revenue tailwind against the $1.13B bar and slight margin dilution.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. A revenue beat in Q2 2026 ($1.10B vs $1.07B) came with +4.55%, but EBITDA and guide drove that move.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mechanical and small. Whether consensus includes it is unknown, and the contribution is about 1% of revenue with almost no EBITDA, so it cannot move the stock on its own.
findings.independence: The closing date and terms are in the NCS 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001692427/000119312526377638/d534761d8k.htm).

findings.finding: On Oct 8, 2026, Equinor extended several existing WFRD agreements by two years and named WFRD primary completion-systems provider for the Statfjord and Oseberg fields on the Norwegian shelf (value undisclosed). The Norway oil-service strike that WFRD flagged as a Q3 drag ran Jun 15 to Jul 14 and ended in arbitration, so its Q3 effect was limited to two weeks and sits inside the Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Contract announcements have not been isolated reaction lines for this name. Europe/SSA/Russia was its only growing segment in Q2 (+10% q/q to $257M).
findings.why_not_priced: The award is public, so the announcement itself is priced. What may not be priced is its use on the call as support for the 2027 international view. Value undisclosed, so small.
findings.independence: The strike end date is from OE Digital (https://www.oedigital.com/news/541213-strike-ends-for-norway-oil-service-workers). The strike's Q3 impact was guided on the Jul 21 call.

findings.finding: Expectations into the print are low. The stock fell from $97.77 (Aug 31, the NCS merger reference close) to $78.6 (-20%). Goldman, Piper, Citi and UBS all cut targets between Sep 23 and Oct 19 while keeping ratings. Short interest is moderate at 5.95% of float and 4.0 days, and skew is balanced at +1.84. The name closed up after 6 of its last 7 prints, including after a $0.35 GAAP EPS miss in July.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference about positioning, not a company number. The drawdown has visible sector causes (crude moves, a 10-07 rate-driven oilfield-services selloff), so part of it is beta rather than WFRD-specific disappointment. Sized small.
findings.independence: Short interest: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/WFRD/short-interest/. Sector selloff: https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/wfrd/news/why-up-down/weatherford-and-highpeak-energy-shares-plummet-what-you-need-to-know (that one is dated June 24).

findings.finding: Q3 adjusted FCF guide is >$100M, and management called Pemex collections 'the biggest driver of variability'. No Q2/Q3 2026 Pemex supplier-payment total is public. Pemex reported paying >152bn pesos in Q1 2026, and on Sep 23, 2026 the AMESPAC suppliers' group said some suppliers still could not invoice commitments up to two years old.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 FCF of $139M (+64% q/q), on Pemex collections, came with +4.55%. Q3 2025, with no Pemex payments in the quarter: +0.64%.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no Q3 Pemex payment series, so neither the market nor I can see it. This is a regional proxy about old arrears and is sized near zero. It is filed because FCF is a line this stock has paid for.
findings.independence: WFRD's Jul 21 call: three straight quarters of sizable Mexico collections, 'cautiously optimistic' (https://www.webull.com/news/15271277430924288). That points the other way.

outside_window.finding: SLB reports Q3 2026 on Oct 23. Its Q2 10-Q showed Middle East revenue -13% q/q, and it warned a renewed escalation could cost ~$150M of Q3 revenue. That peer read-through lands after WFRD's window.
The Delaware redomestication, worth $20-30M of annual savings from 2027, still needs Irish High Court approval. The court date was not found and is not known to fall in the window.
